summary: The dhcp suite's lease on the e1000: os-real takes its lease with ifup -a and reaches the gateway, under tests/cases/machine/dhcp_scenario.c

cases.behavior: os-real booted with no address on the e1000 takes the lease of 192.168.90.20 with ifup -a, with its mask, broadcast address and name server, reaches the gateway by IP and by ARP, and sends a packet off the subnet to the gateway

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine if it still runs, and removes the evidence after a pass

steps.does: boot os-real with rach2.ip=none on 192.168.90.0/24, its card's frames recorded, and log in as root at the console
ask ifconfig whether eth0 has no address
run ifup -a and read the lease, the address, the broadcast address, the mask and /etc/resolv.conf
ping the gateway, arping it and an address nothing answers, read the ARP cache, and ping 10.9.9.9, which is off the subnet
end the machine through QMP and run pcapcheck bcast on its card's frames for the route to 10.9.9.9

assertions.checks: eth0 has the address 0.0.0.0 before userland configures it
ifup -a exits 0, udhcpc says `lease of 192.168.90.20 obtained`, and the kernel says `net: eth0: IPv4 192.168.90.20/`
ifconfig shows the address 192.168.90.20, the broadcast address 192.168.90.255 and the mask 255.255.255.0, and /etc/resolv.conf names 192.168.90.3
a ping of the gateway, 192.168.90.2, is answered
arping -f of the gateway exits 0 with `Received 1 response`
arping of 192.168.90.9, which nothing answers, ends at its deadline with status 1 and `Received 0 response`, which needs the interval timer
the gateway is in the ARP cache
pcapcheck finds the packet for 10.9.9.9 sent to the gateway's hardware address, which is what the leased default route means

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case gives the card a user network of its own with a DHCP server, and reads QEMU's capture of the card; the Lenovo's lease is checked by the release's metal_accept.sh
